source_record.prompt: Make a bounded wardrobe edit to the supplied accepted historical illustration. Preserve every recognizable face, apparent age, eye color, gaze, expression, facial anatomy, natural body fullness, hand and finger positions, action, composition, room and light. Do not slim Emma, change pregnancy/postpartum appearance, or replace anyone with a new actor. The supplied master-derived face is identity evidence, not an instruction to copy one later outfit into every year. Change only the specified clothes and arranged hair; preserve hair color and hairline exactly. Clothing is a researched period-plausible interpretation, not a claim the named people personally owned these precise garments. Natural photographic cloth and folds, no fashion-magazine styling, modern fasteners or modern hat. No text or new scene props. Preserve original input; this replacement does not add a second original count. Early1828, Joseph22 and Emma23. Keep supported pregnancy fullness and exact writing action. Emma wears a modest pale oatmeal cotton morning dress with tiny subdued brown printed motif, an1820s raised waist accommodating pregnancy, sleeves naturally full toward upper arm and tapering to wrists, simple high neckline; replace copied blue later formal dress, oversized later sleeve treatment, ornamental brooch and lace collar. Her same dark hair is neatly pinned back with soft restrained side arrangement, not matching long ceremonial ringlets. Joseph's partly visible clothing becomes a plain warm-gray waistcoat and light shirt with modest neckcloth rather than a black formalcoat; preserve partial-body framing and keep all translation apparatus absent.
source_record.source_limits: Period garment categories/forms only; exact individual colors, cloth, hairstyle and possession not documented. Garment references do not authorize body measurement claims.
